  "title": "U.S. Data Center Capacity: Your seat is skewing your numbers. Five ways to forecast DC capacity (and our definitive view)",
  "type": "sector",
  "priority": "high",
  "published": "2026-11-02",
  "insights": [
   "Bernstein forecasts U.S. installed data center capacity to reach 149 IT-GW by 2030, representing a 4.5x increase from 2025 levels.",

  "title": "US Networking: Connecting the dots... A primer on networking equipment in the age of AI",
  "type": "sector",

  "insights": [
   "Networking has re-rated from a low-growth, service-provider-exposed subsector to a structural AI winner due to the 'bandwidth wall' created by compute performance outpacing network scaling.",
   "AI data center architectures are evolving into four distinct categories: scale-up (within rack), scale-out (between racks), scale-across (between data centers), and scale-in (connecting end users to compute).",
   "Scale-across is a significant emerging revenue opportunity, with estimates suggesting a $8-10B market by 2029, driven by the need to cluster separate data centers for massive training runs.",
   "Hyperscaler demand is the primary growth driver, with networking components representing the most expensive portion of an AI server rack's bill of materials.",

  "insights": [
   "HBF (High-Bandwidth Flash) is a new NAND-based memory tier designed to solve the AI memory wall by providing HBM-like read bandwidth with 8-16x higher capacity at a lower cost per GB.",
   "HBF acts as a capacity-tier backing HBM, storing model weights and reusable KV cache, which reduces the need for expensive GPU/HBM capacity and avoids costly recomputation.",
   "The technology is highly accretive to NAND industry dynamics; it consumes ~6.5x more wafer capacity per bit than conventional TLC NAND, which should tighten supply and support pricing.",
   "Sandisk is the primary driver of HBF, with a roadmap targeting first inference-product samples in 2027 and a second generation for edge AI.",
   "Adoption faces significant hurdles, notably the lack of endorsement from NVIDIA, which is instead promoting alternative solutions like Storage Next and CMX.",
   "HBF is a complement to HBM rather than a replacement, as HBM remains necessary for latency-sensitive, write-intensive active working sets.",
   "The HBF ecosystem includes SK Hynix, Google, Meta, and Tenstorrent, but the absence of TSMC and KIOXIA support remains a notable risk."
